transcript.text: Radio 1 with the Midnight Runner Show. That's starting 9.30 Saturday night. And moving non-stop to the witching hour. With ex-Buzzcocks Pete Shelley in session. And live the Electric Light Orchestra. Just remember that's 9.30 Saturday. On Radio 1 for radio that does not sleep. The Midnight Runner Show.
Action! Radio! Radio Barn!
I don't know if you've heard so far, I thought I'd better slip this in,
the line-up so far for Donington is looking really excellent.
Rumours abound that it is, and I'm sure you know anyway,
Ozzy Osbourne, top of the bill, Scorpions are on the bill as well,
Warlock from Germany, excellent band, and Def Leppard.
That's what everybody's saying about Donington this year.
Ozzy, Scorpions, Warlock and Def Leppard
And two more bands to be announced
Just as soon as we get to know
We'll let you know
Right, time to lie back and enjoy it
And the letter this week
Who puts the music on the turntables
Is from Neil Robinson
Of Fairfield Road, Jasmine, Newcastle upon Tyne
He says, Dear Thomas, I hereby present to you
20 odd minutes of music guaranteed to make you listen
He goes on to say, this is Neil
Please donate the dough to Leukemia Research
which I'm happy to do, so that others don't suffer like my dad did
until his merciful release on April the 12th.
Well, I hope your family's okay now. I really do.
You've gotten over the shock.
Leo Robinson invites you now to lie back and enjoy it.
Four tracks, each one.
[Music]
[Music]
[Music]
[Music]
And of course, knocking at your back door, the 12-inch version.
That was the extended version.
Which, Neil says this, purple from the more modern Perfect Strangers LP,
complete with a perfectly controlled riff from Ritchie Blackmore,
the world's second greatest guitarist.
The 4D Purple, Wasp, Wildchild, their current single.
Not normally a fan of solid thrash type metal, says Neil Robinson,
but this one really made me sit up and want to take a bite out of the furniture.
Status Quo from back in 1974 from the album Quo, the track The Lonely Man.
And Neil says, if this had been a single instead of just being on the Quo album,
it would have been to Quo what Stairway to Heaven was to Led Zeppelin.
Nevertheless, it is, in my humble opinion, the greatest song ever written.
And those three chords are nowhere to be seen.
Start it off with Whitesnake from 1971 from the album Come and Get It.
Just a brilliant song. Classic Whitesnake.
Tony Marsden. It's that solo. My ears just hit the wall.
Neil Robinson, you can take him off the wall, mate.
Thank you very much indeed for that selection. Excellent.
The £12 will go to Leukemia Research.
Good luck to you, mate. And to the rest of your family as well.
It's exactly a quarter past eleven.
This is the Friday Rock Show from BBC Radio 1.
A few mentions now.
Say hi to Adam Evans of Ellesmere Road, Berkhampton.
And tell him even if he doesn't care much for his girlfriend material, I still love him.
That was from Michelle Cartwright.
Or Philip Turner of Romilly in Cheshire.
He says, dear TV, I'll be as old as Dave Lee Travis today.
Ah, well, I'm a fuzeler.
Don't worry about a thing.
How about celebrating the birthday of somebody who's missed only one Friday rock show
by playing Man Erg by Van de Graaff Generator?
Well, you've got them behind me now, not with Man Erg, but with Theme One.
And I have taken note of what you put in your letter,
and I'll pass the suggestions on to Mr. Wilson, our noble producer.
Chris Kent, happy birthday.
For a couple of days ago, how are you doing there in South Sea?
Dear Thomas, says Nancy, here's your roving rock reporter in Reykjavik in Iceland.
Haven't found any Icelandic bands yet, apart from Mezzoforte.
Dave, names like The Eruptions or Hot Lava would sound better.
Don't you agree?
Listen to the program and a certain person in deepest Hampshire.
Will I be listening to Rush and Pink Floyd and Camel on my headphones in these wintry wastes?
When she wrote this, it was minus two degrees centigrade in Arekiewic.
Nancy says hello to that person.
She says what it's all about.
Right, the Huronade album is coming out soon.
On the album, there are tracks by Kiss, Rush, Dio, Scorpions, Jimi Hendrix, Y&T, Accept and Motorhead.
Here are two of them.
First Accept, and then Motorhead, Motorhead.
